extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and scholastic contest judges (WJEA)
extracted.subtask_short: breaking news writing for scholastic contests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for identifying, reporting, and judging breaking-news stories in scholastic journalism contests, emphasizing immediacy, verification, and public significance. Intended to help students determine what counts as breaking news and how to handle live/updating coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just happened (within hours, not days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it just happened — within hours, not days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes extreme recency; stories that are several days old generally do not qualify as breaking news for contest purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demands immediate audience attention
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it demands immediate audience attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the audience needs to know now (safety alerts, ongoing threats, time-sensitive outcomes) rather than later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfolding — facts still emerging
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it is unfolding — facts are still emerging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking stories often change; coverage should note uncertainty and update as facts arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unscheduled — could not be planned for
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it is unscheduled — could not be planned for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes unexpected events from planned coverage (e.g., scheduled press conferences may not be 'breaking' unless something sudden occurs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Has potential to change as new information arrives
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it has potential to change as new information arrives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation of change should be signaled in copy (e.g., use caveats) and reporters should follow up with updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of community / national / global significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A story qualifies as breaking news if it is of community, national, or global significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance is relative to the audience; evaluate geographic scope and impact when deciding if something is breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of event types that commonly qualify: Disasters (natural, accidents, attacks); Major crime (shootings, attacks); Deaths of major figures; Major political/government events (resignations, votes); Sports outcomes (championship game ending); Court verdicts in major cases; Stock market crashes/surges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories as examples of typically qualifying events, but apply the other qualifying criteria (recency, significance, unfolding nature) as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify before publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify information before publishing — even if behind competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize confirmation of facts from reliable sources over speed; do not publish unverified claims simply to beat others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing — official sources for facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use official sources for facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on statements from authorities, public agencies, police/fire departments, or direct eyewitness accounts that can be corroborated; attribute sources clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats — use phrases like 'according to,' 'early reports'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use caveats to signal unconfirmed or preliminary information (e.g., 'according to,' 'early reports').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly indicate what is confirmed versus what is preliminary to avoid misleading readers as more information develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates — return to story as facts emerge
rubrics_metrics.description: Return to the story with updates as facts emerge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a visible update history or notice; actively follow evolving details rather than silently editing earlier copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections — promptly fix errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly fix errors via corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge mistakes openly and correct the record quickly; transparency maintains credibility in fast-moving coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid speculation in breaking-news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not offer unverified theories or conjecture; clearly separate verified facts from expert opinion when included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish what's confirmed vs. reported elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish what is confirmed by your reporting versus what has been reported elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute secondary reports and do not present others' unverified reporting as confirmed fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify deaths only after family notified when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify deaths only after family notified when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise sensitivity and verification before naming deceased individuals; follow ethical and legal considerations around identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency (most extreme version)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: extreme recency is central to breaking news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how recently the event occurred; more recent events are more likely to qualify as breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude of immediate impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: consider the magnitude of the event's immediate impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger-scale effects (many people affected, significant disruption) increase newsworthiness as breaking news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public safety implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: whether the event has public safety implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events that affect public safety (ongoing threats, hazards, evacuations) are high priority for breaking coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: the geographic relevance to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local versus national/global relevance matters; a locally disruptive event can be breaking news for that community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: speed/velocity at which information is developing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-velocity situations that change rapidly require distinct handling (frequent updates, caveats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience curiosity / urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: degree of audience curiosity or urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether readers/viewers are likely to seek immediate information about the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disruption to normal life
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: whether the event disrupts normal life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures, transport impacts, service interruptions, or other disruptions increase breaking-news relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political / institutional significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: political or institutional importance of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level resignations, votes, or institutional actions can qualify as breaking news due to their systemic implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic / video potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: presence of strong photographic or video elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual immediacy can raise an event's profile as breaking news; prioritize verified visual material and attribute sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality > Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice reminder: Quality over Speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice accuracy, context, or clarity solely to be first; better reporting trumps being first with errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification > Scoop
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice reminder: Verification over Scoop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm facts before publishing even if it means losing the scoop; unchecked scoops damage credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution > Sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice reminder: Caution over Sensationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensational language or hype; maintain measured, factual tone in breaking coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update notices > Quiet edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice reminder: Use visible update notices rather than quiet edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it clear when a story has been updated and what changed to keep readers informed about evolving facts.
